spawn_agent.description: Create an independent agent from a preset. Send its task separately after the creation result. Delegate complex work; capability_manager may only develop capabilities.

spawned.description: Whether the new agent instance was created.

parent_id.description: Identifier of the parent agent, or null for the root.

send_message_to_agent.description: Send a message or task to another agent; every agent can communicate. The recipient receives message_from_agent.

text.description: Text content to process; see the action or event description.

delivered.description: Whether the recipient accepted the message into its queue.

list_agents.description: Inspect live agent instances before addressing or managing them.

get_agent.description: Inspect the current preset base, individual additions and computed effective configuration separately.

parent_id.description: Identifier of the parent agent, or null for the root.

edit_agent.description: Change individual additions only: additional_instructions, capabilities_add, capabilities_remove and model (null clears the override). Mandatory preset capabilities cannot be removed. History is preserved.

changes.description: Partial update: additional_instructions string, capabilities_add/remove arrays of IDs, model string or null. Omitted fields remain unchanged.

interrupt_agent.description: Cancel the current generation; keep history, queued events and already running actions.

delete_agent.description: Delete an agent and all descendants, stop their executions and erase all instance data without late saves recreating it.

deleted.description: Whether the agent and its descendants were deleted.

list_agent_presets.description: list_agent_presets: manage the live mandatory preset base. Updates apply to existing instances without clearing history; removal recursively deletes all instances and descendants. Only main may perform this operation.

presets.description: Saved presets and their initial assignments.

get_preset.description: get_preset: manage the live mandatory preset base. Updates apply to existing instances without clearing history; removal recursively deletes all instances and descendants. Only main may perform this operation.

create_preset.description: create_preset: manage the live mandatory preset base. Updates apply to existing instances without clearing history; removal recursively deletes all instances and descendants. Only main may perform this operation.

error.description: Failure details if the operation did not succeed.

edit_preset.description: edit_preset: manage the live mandatory preset base. Updates apply to existing instances without clearing history; removal recursively deletes all instances and descendants. Only main may perform this operation.

changes.description: Partial update: person, model (null inherits Jarvis default), capabilities or capabilities_add/remove. Omitted fields remain unchanged.

error.description: Failure details if the operation did not succeed.

remove_preset.description: remove_preset: manage the live mandatory preset base. Updates apply to existing instances without clearing history; removal recursively deletes all instances and descendants. Only main may perform this operation.

error.description: Failure details if the operation did not succeed.

list_capabilities.description: list_capabilities: inspect or manage capabilities by their globally unique ID. Modules are assigned whole. Preset capabilities are mandatory; only individual additions may be removed. Global pause affects user capabilities, not built-ins. Wait for pause result before resuming, never toggle the same ID twice in one batch.

actions.description: Standalone action identifiers assigned to the agent.

handlers.description: Standalone observer identifiers assigned to the agent.

modules.description: Module identifiers assigned to the agent.

enabled.description: Whether the capability is locally enabled for the agent.

memory_write.description: Write a message from your past self to your future self in semantic memory. Record one confirmed, self-contained fact likely to remain true in the near future: a person's stable habits, character, preferences, interests, biography or relationships, or persistent information about devices and surroundings. State the established fact directly, with enough context to understand it later. Do not record uncertain inferences, hypothetical possibilities, plans as completed events, current tasks, temporary projects or short-lived states. Do not infer a habit from one observation or duplicate an existing entry, PERSON or ENVIRONMENT. The core generates the entry ID.

content.description: One short, self-contained message to your future self stating a confirmed fact expected to remain stable in the near future. Include whom or what the fact concerns; exclude uncertainty, hypothetical plans, current tasks and temporary states.

id.description: Generated ID of the saved semantic memory entry; use the ID currently shown in MEMORY for later editing or deletion.

memory_edit.description: Replace the complete text of an existing semantic memory entry by its ID. Write a clear message to your future self containing the corrected, confirmed and sufficiently stable fact. Preserve relevant established information; do not turn possibilities, intentions or uncertain conclusions into facts.

id.description: Exact ID of the existing MEMORY entry to replace.

content.description: Complete replacement message to your future self, stating the corrected confirmed and stable information clearly enough to understand without the current conversation.

status.description: Operation result; updated means the identified memory entry was replaced.

memory_delete.description: Delete a semantic memory entry by its ID when its information is false, obsolete, duplicated or no longer suitable as a confirmed stable message to your future self.

id.description: Exact ID of the MEMORY entry that should be removed permanently.

status.description: Operation result; deleted means the identified memory entry was removed.

reply.description: Send the exact text to the human interlocutor through the console response channel. This capability is offered when voice output is unavailable because the configured speech executable is absent. The text appears inside the protocol trace.

text.description: Exact user-facing text to return through the fallback console response.

status.description: Operation result; successful means the fallback reply was emitted.

no_action.description: End the current reasoning cycle and wait for new events when no available action is appropriate. This invocation uses a unique call_id like other actions, must be the only action in the response, and does not produce a call_result.

speech.description: Speak the supplied text directly to the human interlocutor using Fish Audio S2 Pro. Provide the exact utterance ready for pronunciation: direct speech, numbers written as spoken words, natural punctuation and correct ё in Russian. Expand notation and abbreviations when necessary for natural speech. S2 Pro supports inline delivery instructions in square brackets, placed where the vocal change should occur: [whisper], [short pause], [emphasis], [chuckle] and [sigh]. Tags can also contain natural-language instructions, such as [professional broadcast tone]. Use them when they suit the intended delivery. Apart from these supported vocal tags, omit labels, stage directions, Markdown and commentary about the utterance. The result reports completed or interrupted playback.

text.description: Exact direct speech for Fish Audio S2 Pro, ready to pronounce, with numbers written as spoken words and correct ё in Russian. Inline square-bracket tags may guide delivery, for example: [short pause] Сейчас проверю, сэр.

status.description: Playback result; successful means the utterance finished. interrupted means the user stopped it by speaking; this result arrives together with the recognized user utterance, before its speech_detected event.

structure_error.description: The previous response was rejected because its JSON or action arguments violated the protocol. Read the validation details and return a corrected response using fresh call_id values for every invocation. A rejected call_id remains occupied in the context.

code.description: Machine-readable error code identifying the class of structural validation failure.

message.description: Human-readable validation details explaining what was invalid and what must be corrected.

response.description: Your original rejected model response; inspect it to correct the structure without repeating the same invalid output.

message_from_agent.description: A direct message from another agent. from_agent_id and from_name identify the sender; text contains their message or task.

text.description: Text content to process; see the action or event description.

system_started.description: The system has started. This event gives you an opportunity to take initiative: consider your personality, available capabilities and current context, then independently choose a useful action or begin an interaction. Initiative is welcome but no specific action is mandatory. datetime is the local startup time with timezone.

datetime.description: Exact local startup date and time in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.

capability_error.description: A capability has failed. The kind, ID and error describe the failure; call_id identifies an affected invocation when available. Determine the actual outcome from these details before retrying, choosing another capability or reporting the issue.

kind.description: Kind of capability that failed: module, standalone action, or standalone handler.

id.description: Identifier of the capability in which the unhandled failure occurred.

error.description: Failure details to inspect when deciding how to recover or what to report.

call_id.description: Invocation ID associated with the failure when one specific action call was affected; use it to correlate the error with your prior request.

speech_detected.description: A human interlocutor's utterance recognized from microphone audio. The text may contain transcription errors; interpret it in the ongoing conversation and resolve meaningful ambiguity when necessary.

text.description: Recognized text of the user's spoken utterance; it may contain speech-recognition errors or spoken-form wording.

capability_development.description: Develop capabilities using file and bash tools. Relative paths and default cwd are bound to the capability storage directory. All four tools are assigned together.

capability_development.read_file.description: Read numbered UTF-8 text or native image/audio/video/file attachments. Optional lines are inclusive and 1-based. Relative paths use this tool's base directory.

start_line.description: First included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file beginning.

end_line.description: Last included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file end.

start_line.description: First included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file beginning.

end_line.description: Last included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file end.

content.description: Text content of the file or replacement range.

capability_development.write_file.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 file, creating parent directories. Relative paths use this tool's base directory.

content.description: Text content of the file or replacement range.

written.description: Whether the file was written successfully.

capability_development.edit_file.description: Replace an inclusive 1-based line range; invalid ranges fail without editing. Relative paths use this tool's base directory.

start_line.description: First included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file beginning.

end_line.description: Last included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file end.

content.description: Text content of the file or replacement range.

edited.description: Whether the requested range or object was edited successfully.

capability_development.execute_command.description: Run one non-interactive bash command without a result timeout. Every invocation starts a fresh shell; cwd, exports and shell state never carry between calls. Omitted cwd uses this tool's base directory. Return full exit_code, stdout and stderr.

command.description: One non-interactive bash command to execute.

cwd.description: Working directory; omitted or null uses the project root.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the completed command.

stdout.description: Captured standard output of the command.

stderr.description: Captured standard error of the command.
